i agree with removing the me designation from cfsme. then patients could decide on a better name than cfs. dividing us up has been a hurtful issue for a long time. we must stay on the side of love, tolerance, acceptance, inclusion against the exercise of control over us all.

Name: 17970_sws_cb1_endocannabinoids_rem
Representative_Docs: first, some terms: cb1 = cannabinoid receptor . key part of endocannabinoid system (ecs). activated by thc. sws = slow wave sleep. this is "deep" phase of sleep w/o vivid dreaming, important for restoration. paradoxical sleep (ps) = rem sleep in humans, when we dream. /

in animals, direct activation of cb1 with drugs increases sws by stabilizing and increasing the length of individual bouts of sws that animals cycle through while sleeping. activation of cb1 has opposite effect on rem sleep, w/ cb1 activation leading to less rem. /

in general, animal studies indicate that endocannabinoids are important for "sleep stability," i.e. ability to stay asleep and cycle through sws + rem normally. genetically engineered mice w/o cb1 receptors have reduced and fragmented sleep, and spend more time awake. /

Name: 18144_residuals_normality_lognormal_rmse
Representative_Docs: normality of residuals is not a measure of fit. stick to raw for interpretability unless relationship is on log scale (even then you can exponent your results for interpretability). use bootstrap/permutation tests for inference and dont worry about distribution of the residuals.

Name: 18332_n1_variance_overoptimizing_variancen
Representative_Docs: i.e., the sample mean is the value around which the variance is *minimized*. then you compute the sample variance. but then you realize that the sample mean itself is not where the /population/'s variance is minimized; that is around the population mean.

when you compute variance without dividing by the actual unique info in the sample (n-1), you therefore balance around an estimate, not a population. each var estimate is wrt to a random mean, and not to mu. the correction effectively 'adds back' the mean variance.

to me, the problem is simply that we use the sample mean, while we should use the population mean. so we need to correct for the difference between the sample mean and the population mean, which is given by variance/n.

Name: 19545_fitness_optimising_reproductionmaximizing_fitnessmaximizing
Representative_Docs: at the end of ontogeny fitness is accrued depending on how well the organism matches its environment across adulthood. if we assume a relatively stable environment across adulthood an organism trades off plasticity with the ability to develop a highly specialized phenotype.

i think this makes sense if we are thinking broadly, but when we frame the problem computationally its still useful to say the say the process is optimising fitness. lets consider a simple optimization problem, wherein a variable x directly dictates an organisms fitness.

so i get why one might say evolution is not optimising fitness, but rather is optimising proxies for fitness. however, when we model the impossibility of achieving the best fitness value is usually inherently taken into account.

Name: 20361_mict_hiit_intensity_highintensity
Representative_Docs: next, and this is absolutely crucial. check when the participants were asked to report their pleasure-displeasure. if the mict participants were asked during exercise but the hiit participants were asked after the high-intensity intervals, this is the most clear sign of bias.

never (ever!) accept overall means of heart rate or oxygen uptake over the entire bouts. these data are recorded continuously and must be reported as such. it's possible that, by the end, due to creep, the intensity of mict was equal or higher than the intensity of hiit intervals

dr lubans: my point was that low hiit intensity + high mict intensity leads to misleading affective results. i have examples were, due to drift, "mict" intensity > hiit intensity! plus, some think that % hrpeak will maintain the claimed hiit physiol effects; obviously, it won't
